title: Reactogenicity and safety of the human rotavirus vaccine, Rotarix™ in The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India: a post-marketing surveillance study.
ehr_evidence: Baseline demographic data was reported on the case report form by the investigators at the time of enrolment/first visit. AEs were recorded on diary cards after each vaccine dose.
summary: Post-marketing surveillance study evaluating the reactogenicity and safety of the Rotarix™ rotavirus vaccine in healthy infants across The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India.
key_findings: In The Philippines, 14.7% (95% CI: 12.9–16.7) of infants reported at least one Grade 2/3 solicited adverse event, with irritability most common (32.2% post-Dose-1; 23.5% post-Dose-2).
In Sri Lanka, 14.9% (95% CI: 12.0–18.3) reported Grade 2/3 solicited AEs, with fever most common (18.0% post-Dose-1; 20.2% post-Dose-2).
In India, 12.7% (95% CI: 9.3–16.7) reported Grade 2/3 solicited AEs, with irritability most common (23.0% post-Dose-1; 13.2% post-Dose-2).
Unsolicited AEs were reported in 24.5% of infants in The Philippines, 4.8% in Sri Lanka, and 6.9% in India.
Forty-one serious adverse events occurred in The Philippines, with six in four infants considered causally related to vaccination; no SAEs were reported in Sri Lanka or India.
captured_features: solicited adverse events (fever, vomiting, diarrhea, irritability, cough/runny nose, loss of appetite)
study_design: open, single-group, multi-center post-marketing surveillance study
population: healthy infants aged at least 6 weeks at first dose in The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India
limitations: low sample size limiting detection of rare AEs
passive reporting leading to potential underreporting of AEs and SAEs
loss to follow-up for the infant who developed intussusception
